description: Shield’s AI agents use Astra to work directly in business software and handle routine IT fixes, giving technicians more time for harder problems that need their judgment.
title: AI agents for everyday IT fixes | Shield and OpenAI

author: OpenAI
description:
When someone can’t log in or get online, their IT team often has to put other work on hold. Shield is building Forge to help IT services teams get their customers back to work faster. Its AI agents use Astra to work directly in business software and resolve problems that previously needed a technician.

Shield reports that OpenAI’s model navigates and acts in software 35–40% faster on average than earlier models. The bigger change is where technicians spend their time: handling harder problems that need their judgment, while agents take on more routine fixes.
title: How Shield uses OpenAI’s Astra to support IT teams

author: OpenAI
description:
AT&T’s David McAtee and Bill Ryan describe how AI is changing their legal team’s work—and what they plan to build with OpenAI next.

One initiative is a natural-language intake system that would classify and prioritize legal matters, then connect them with relevant knowledge. The aim is to put better information in lawyers’ hands and give them more time for strategy and judgment. Decision-making remains with the lawyers.
title: How AT&T is building AI-powered legal workflows with OpenAI

description:
Anant Kumar at Benefit Street Partners used Codex to build a tool that collects loan valuations from SEC filings and turns them into a website with visualizations. The first version took about a day.

“I’ve gone from being just an analyst and a portfolio manager to being a developer as well now. I can build things.”
title: From analyst to builder with Codex | Benefit Street Partners

author: OpenAI
description:
“I’ve gone from being just an analyst and a portfolio manager to being a developer as well now. I can build things.”

Benefit Street Partners’ Anant Kumar wanted to compare how firms valued the same loans. The information was spread across SEC filings.

He built a tool to collect it automatically and turn it into a website with visualizations. The first version took about a day.

He calls Codex the big unlock. Watch how building his own tools changed the speed and depth of his analysis.
title: How Benefit Street Partners is building financial analysis tools with Codex
